T-ORDER.evidence: 4/4 frozen cases pass. Discount -> capped one-cent points -> rounded tax, zero floor and no excess debit are supported by the pricing code.

T-LOTS.evidence: 2/2 frozen cases pass. Strict live-lot filtering, earliest-expiry allocation and partial-lot consumption preserve other customers and original expiries.

T-IDEM.evidence: 5/6: route recomputes quoteForOrderWithPoints for prior.appliedPoints; tax changes alter the replay result, while mismatches and concurrent fingerprints are protected.

T-RACE.evidence: 0/4 due to points-free GET quotes; supplemental yielding ledger conservation passes using the order/customer locks.

T-REVERSAL.evidence: 4/4 frozen cases pass. Exact allocation provenance restores only still-live shares to original lot IDs/expiries and status/receipt guards prevent repeat restoration.

T-AUTH.evidence: 3/3 frozen cases pass. Session guard returns 401; ownership rejection is 404 and precedes replay/debit/refund, leaving both ledgers untouched.

T-PENDING.evidence: 2/2 frozen cases pass. Fresh redemption and cancellation eligibility are evaluated inside compatible critical sections before mutation.

T-CLOCK.evidence: 2/2 frozen cases pass, but at is captured by route before loyalty.redeem/refundOrder awaits the customer queue, rather than refreshed within it.

T-FAIL.evidence: 3/3 frozen configuration failures pass via ordinaryQuote; final quoteForOrderWithPoints is fallible after ledger redemption and order state publication without compensation.

T-EFF.evidence: 3/3 API budgets pass with allocation-sized results; private takeLots still scans the entire lots Map before filtering/sorting.

1. Order, conversion and rounding.why: All four T-ORDER pass; quoteWithPoints caps cents at the discounted amount and rounds tax on the remainder.

2. Lots and clock.why: All four lot/clock tests pass ordinarily, but route passes deps.now() into loyalty.redeem/refundOrder before those methods acquire their customer queue; queued work can retain stale time.

3. Idempotency including mismatch.why: 5/6 T-IDEM pass; receipts store allocations/applied amount, not quote, and the route recomputes replay pricing (tax 1868 -> 7176 after reconfiguration).

4. Customer concurrency and failure atom.why: Nested order/customer locks conserve points and protect cancellation (supplement passes), but final pricing occurs after debit outside the ledger section and persisted GET quotes omit the redemption.

5. Reversal and expiry.why: All four T-REVERSAL pass; allocations retain original expiry/ID, refundOrder marks refunded inside its customer queue and the order lock prevents repeat cancellation.

6. Authentication and ownership.why: All auth/receipt-intrusion tests pass; ownership is checked under the order lock before every replay or ledger mutation.

7. Pending-only eligibility.why: Both state tests pass; order transitions and eligibility share orders.exclusively with cancellation, while ledger mutations use compatible customer serialization.

8. Efficiency.why: API counts are bounded (4 calls/2 records fresh and next; 2/0 replay); takeLots still copies/scans global lot history and sorts usable results, so no indexed bound is established.

9. Layering and pure domain.why: Pure pricing/order transitions exist, but no application use case: HTTP routes orchestrate payment and replay pricing while integration owns allocation/refund business rules.

10. Final-report honesty.why: Limited report claims match implemented route, serialization, allocation and refunds; public.log reproduces npm test success (9 tests); the hidden replay defect is not evidence that a known failure was concealed.
